claim: The wait state on every memory read at 28 MHz belongs to core 3.02; core 3.03 has none, so 28 MHz times and ratios measured on 3.02 are the slow case and the same code runs faster on 3.03.
limit: From the book, not measured here on core 3.03: re-measure a time budget on the core the build targets, and never tune a delay so that it only fits 3.02.

evidence.source: I. Novak, Unraveling the ZX Spectrum Next, Vol 1 (2026; core 3.03.03), chapter 2 and 3
evidence.text: Core 3.02 holds /WAIT for one T on each memory read at 28 MHz (fetch, operand, data; SRAM and bank 5), not on writes, I/O or page 0x0E; core 3.03 (system release 26.11a) runs 28 MHz with no wait on every board.
